title: Physics and other sciences
competency: Explain how physics relates to chemistry, biology, astronomy and geology.

en.text: Physics and chemistry both study matter and its interaction with energy. Atomic and subatomic physics explains how atoms bond. The physics of heat tells whether a reaction can happen. Spectroscopy, the study of how matter and radiation interact, is a tool both sciences share.

screens.title: Salt from sea water
screens.ask: You boil salty water until it is dry. Salt stays behind. Which physics idea explains this?
opts: Change of state: water evaporates, salt does not
screens.after: Heat gives water molecules enough energy to escape as vapour. Salt has a far higher boiling point, so it stays.

screens.title: Spectroscopy
paras: Spectroscopy studies how matter and electromagnetic radiation interact, by wavelength or frequency.
Most of what we know about atoms and molecules comes from it.
Chemistry is rooted in atomic and molecular physics.

items: Each element absorbs or emits its own wavelengths: its fingerprint.
The pattern of scattered X-rays shows how atoms are arranged in a crystal.
Electric and magnetic fields sort ions by mass.
Shows the energy given out or taken in by a reaction.

en.text: Physics explains how living things work. A body is stable when its centre of gravity is over its base of support. Soft animals like the earthworm move using Pascal's principle. Our voice is sound from vibrating vocal cords when we breathe out, nerves carry electrical pulses, and light (400–700 nm) drives vision and photosynthesis.

screens.title: One foot or two?
screens.ask: Why is it harder to stand on one foot than on two?
opts: The base of support is smaller
You weigh more on one foot
screens.after: A small base lets the centre of gravity slip outside it easily, so the body tips.

screens.title: Mechanics and the body
paras: A body is stable if its centre of mass is directly over its base of support.
If the centre of mass moves outside the base, its weight makes a torque that tips the body.
A wider base and a lower centre of gravity make a body more stable.

en.text: Astronomers learn about far objects only from the radiation they send. Gravity gives the centripetal force for orbits. Each kind of telescope detects one band of the spectrum. Brightness falls with distance²; a light year is the distance light travels in a year (about 9.46 × 10¹² km). Electrons jumping down emit light, jumping up absorb it. Geologists use waves, magnetism, density and radioactivity to study rocks.
